text:
maya: Heads-up: Sigma reported streaming regen failures right after we flipped 2.3 at 09:12 PT. Customer SLA says immediate attention. They see aborted streams ~10% of the time on long-regens.

devon: Can you share a sample trace? stack or runtime log?

maya: Pasted snippet: `2024-02-15T16:12:41Z runtime ERR: stream aborted: upstream closed (kvcache fetch failed) // tokens_out=1324` — consistently happens when tokens_out > ~1200.

sam: That threshold aligns with the new batching+prefetch window we introduced. Suspect a race between the async kv warm path and our stream writer.

liam: How many customers affected? Is this limited to Sigma?

maya: So far only Sigma (heavy long-chat usage). They flagged production errors and request-stepdowns if we can

amelia-csm: Sigma is anxious. They asked: can we avoid seeing any aborted responses in the next 48h? They prefer no rollback but will accept a temporary routing if needed.

jen: Triage options: 1) Hotpatch runtime to add defensive fallback on kv miss (fast), 2) Route Sigma to variant-stable (previous variant) until we patch, 3) Defer to next sprint and patch with longer QA.

devon: I can do (1) today: add sync fallback and a feature flag so we can toggle. Rough ETA: 4h dev + 2h CI + 1h canary.

sam: Is fallback measurable impact on latency/cost?

devon: On regen paths it will add ~8-12% token latency for affected requests. Non-affected calls unchanged.

liam: Given SLA and customer impact I propose hotpatch + canary to Sigma only. If we see >0 errors in 4h, route them to variant-stable and investigate deeper.

maya: Agreed. I'll tell Sigma the plan: attempt a guarded deploy today, will fail open to route if any errors.

jen: Add acceptance criteria: no aborted streams for Sigma for 4h post-canary AND <2% increase in 95p latency. Also require smoke-tests for long-regens in staging.

devon: Will add e2e case (regen length 1500 tokens) and the flag. Also adding a telemetry counter metric: runtime.kvcache.fallback.count and alert threshold >3 in 15m.

sam: Please update the incident playbook: include rollback play `route:sigma->variant-stable` and contact list for Sigma CSM.

ci-bot: Build queued: `runtime#guard-kv-fallback` pipeline id 820.

devon: Build passed, PR up: https://repo/redwood/runtime/pull/820 (summary: add kv sync fallback + feature flag + telemetry). Tagging jen + liam for quick review.

maya: Thanks. Amelia, pinged CSM with tentative window: canary tonight 18:00 PT.

amelia-csm: Noted. Sigma wants a short post-canary summary and rollback window. Also asked if temp routing would change cost or tokens.

jen: We should also capture this as a post-launch follow-up item: add to backlog with priority P1 for deeper root cause and perf optimization (avoid fallback long-term). Create ticket and link to RFC.

sam: I'll create ticket RD-PL-3321 with acceptance: root cause identified + plan to remove fallback within 2 sprints.

liam: If hotpatch works, we still want a targeted regression test in CI for long-regens. Add a nightly canary job that runs one long-regeneration against a canary pool.

devon: Will add canary test and the feature-flag gate.

ci-bot: Canary deploy started to canary group: sigma + internal-canaries. Monitoring dashboards: runtime.streams/errors, runtime.kvcache.fallback.count.

maya: Monitoring looks clean at +30m. No new aborted streams for Sigma so far.

amelia-csm: Sigma acknowledged the canary start and appreciates the quick action.

jen: Keep monitoring for the full 4h window. If it stays green we'll promote and close the emergency. Log follow-up in retro.

liam: If anything spikes, route immediately and escalate to eng-oncall.

devon: Noted. I'll keep an eye on the alerts and post summary once 4h complete.

maya: Thanks everyone. Post-canary notes: add brief to release notes and mark follow-up RD-PL-3321.

ci-bot: Deploy finished: `runtime#guard-kv-fallback` promoted to prod for canary group.
